summary: Two manifests (package.json and requirements.txt) exist, and neither has a lockfile. Three runtime dependencies are unpinned: express and gunicorn have no version constraint, so builds can't be reproduced.

findings.title: express unpinned ("*") with no lockfile
findings.evidence: "express": "*" — any version is accepted and no npm lockfile is committed.
findings.recommendation: Pin express to a specific version, or a reviewed range, and commit a package-lock.json.

findings.title: gunicorn has no version specifier
findings.evidence: `gunicorn` is declared with no version, and no pip lockfile or constraints file exists.
findings.recommendation: Pin gunicorn with `==` to a tested version, or use a lock or constraints file.

limitations: Hygiene only: no OSV lookups were made, so known vulnerabilities were not checked in this step.
The other dependencies are pinned exactly (dayjs 1.11.13, lodash 4.17.15, Flask 3.0.3, requests 2.19.0). They raise no hygiene findings, but the known_vulnerabilities step should check them.
